> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e3b79c3b21a0f453bbd8f4a44762342498a45fab` — the merge of head `b5cbc6ad19fe850a64cb98c4bf553cbbb3d5a128` into base `c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e3b79c3b21a0f453bbd8f4a44762342498a45fab && git checkout e3b79c3b21a0f453bbd8f4a44762342498a45fab
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe b5cbc6ad19fe850a64cb98c4bf553cbbb3d5a128 && git checkout -B drift-repro c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe && git merge --no-ff b5cbc6ad19fe850a64cb98c4bf553cbbb3d5a128

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4cb593b8cc030ec5f5e3acd319ef02a60f754f60`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/credential-change-ends-prior-access.md (declaration lines), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-mailbox-proof.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/credential-change-ends-prior-access.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-one-step-acceptance-34257.test.ts + none in the diff beyond those; read, never reviewed: auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, auth-manager-sign-in-lockout.ts, auth-manager-database-secret.ts, admin-user-endpoints.ts, operator-password-reset.ts, driver-sql sql-driver-column-creation.ts, and better-auth 1.7.12 (api/dispatch, routes/email-verification, routes/update-user, utils/password, db/internal-adapter, plugins/two-factor) read from the published package source
Security-touching: yes

Review face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; no card, by rule). Inputs: the PR body, its eight-file list, the net diff against merge base `eca20d22191`, the check-runs on this head, the dev evidence on this head, and the security seat's private residual file. Nothing was built, run or re-run. `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` is a prose face and is the seat's at ACCEPT.

Gate verdicts on this head (check-run conclusions): Test Core 1/10 to 10/10, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Build Docs, Spec property liveness: all `success`. No check-run concluded `failure`; the skipped ones are the UI, opt-in and queue legs. Dev evidence on this head: plugin-auth 288/288 files, 6046 passed, 10 skipped; dogfood battery command-exit 0, 482 files passed, 3 skipped, no failures; the predicate, the sign-in refusal and the session re-end each turn their cases red when removed.

### ① Derived judgments

The rule: a credential change ends access issued before it. One predicate (`issuedBeforeCredentialChange`, strict "before") over one clock (`readCredentialChangedAt`: `updated_at` of the account's `sys_account` row with provider `credential`; a row written within `FIRST_CREDENTIAL_WINDOW_MS` of its creation, and no row, read as never changed). Every accept-set change the diff implies:

1. `GET /verify-email`, a token carrying `updateTo` whose `iat` falls before the clock: the before-hook replaces the token with a value no signer issued, so the vendor's own `jwtVerify` failure answers `401 INVALID_TOKEN` or the `error=INVALID_TOKEN` redirect. Right. Read against `routes/email-verification.mjs`: the replacement lands before the handler reads `ctx.query.token`, and the hook's return shape is the `context` arm `runBeforeHooks` merges.
2. The same door, both request types: the vendor's confirmation token and its verification token both carry `updateTo`, so both are judged. Right, and wider than the changeset's wording ("the one `POST /change-email` mails to the new address"), in the safe direction.
3. The same door, a token that is both expired and older than the change now answers `INVALID_TOKEN` where it answered `TOKEN_EXPIRED`. Right (it is what a never-issued token answers); unstated in the changeset, and a refusal either way.
4. The same door, same-second tokens: `iat` is whole seconds, so a token minted in the second of the change, after it, is refused. Right and declared.
5. A token without `updateTo`, a token that does not decode, and a token naming no account are left to the vendor. Right: the rule's list names the email-change link only.
6. The early `return` from the global before-hook on an ended link skips the rest of that hook for the request. Right: every later section of the hook is gated on a path other than `/verify-email`, so an ended link and a never-issued one reach the vendor through the same remaining path.
7. `/two-factor/verify-totp`, `/verify-otp`, `/verify-backup-code`: a challenge whose `createdAt` is before the clock is deleted with its attempt counter, and the vendor answers what it answers for no challenge. Right, read against `verify-two-factor.mjs` (cookie name, identifier, `value` is the user id, `2fa-attempts-` prefix).
8. Both reset doors, on success: the account's sessions are ended again after the write, whatever the clock says. Right: `revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset` is fixed `true` in `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts`, so no deployment gains a revocation it had switched off.
9. `/change-password` with `revokeOtherSessions: true`, on success: every session but the one the door installed is ended after the write. Right; without the flag nothing moves, as declared.
10. One-step invitation acceptance for an existing account: sessions ended again after the write, ahead of the session the door opens. Right; the door already ended them before the write.
11. `/sign-in/email` and `/sign-in/phone-number`: when the credential read after the session opened differs from the one read before the vendor's check, or either reading is missing, the session is deleted and the door answers its own wrong-password code (`INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD`, or the phone plugin's `INVALID_PHONE_NUMBER_OR_PASSWORD`). Right. Derived and stated in the PR body: the attempt is settled as a refused credential, so it counts toward the lock and writes its `login_failed` row.
12. Hook order: the refusal runs first in the global after-hook, which `getHooks` places ahead of every plugin after-hook, and it clears `newSession`, so the second-factor after-hook opens no challenge. Right, read against `dispatch.mjs` and `two-factor/index.mjs`.
13. Public surface: no export, schema key, request or response shape moves. `credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts` is imported by three sibling modules and re-exported by none. Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, title `fix(plugin-auth)!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body, a BREAKING paragraph, and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). This matches what the diff publishes: a non-protocol breaking narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition (AGENTS.md, changeset rule). The narrowing takes away no declared capability at a consumer: each refused request gets a code the same door already answers. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` conclude `success` on this head. Level and declaration lines are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No card and no `open_questions`: nothing to answer from that side.
- Dev flag, "no `Fixes` line": right for a seat order with no card.
- Dev flag, three gate commands not measured locally (`check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt`): answered by `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Type Check · debt ledger`, both `success` on this head.
- Dev flag, the session re-end ablation leg: answered by the dev evidence on this head (the leg turns its cases red).
- SQL push-down: no finding. The clock is one `findOne` on two equality predicates with a three-field projection. No in-app join is added. The one new id materialisation is `endSessionsAfterCredentialWrite` with `keep` (list the account's sessions, delete each but one); its reason is given in the docblock (each delete goes through the vendor's adapter so the session-delete hooks run), and the set is one account's live sessions.
- Private residuals held by the security seat: R1, R2 — graded in the seat's private notes. Neither is graded must-fix for this PR.
- Escalated to the seat, not a finding on this diff: the rule sentence in the changeset is bounded by "An account's first password is not a change"; what the clock is when a door creates the local credential is a ruling the seat holds with R1.

### ④ Design judgment

`credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts`: holds against the code it cites. The clock's row is the row every password door writes: `internalAdapter.updatePassword` and `updateAccount` (vendor reset, change and one-step doors), `admin-user-endpoints.ts`, and `operator-password-reset.ts`, which writes `updated_at` itself. Audit timestamps are millisecond or finer on every SQL dialect the driver creates (`DATETIME(3)`, `timestamptz`), so the strict comparison against a millisecond challenge time and a whole-second `iat` behaves as the docblock says. Tried and not broken: an unsigned or repeated `token` parameter (left to the vendor, same answer), a token for an address with no account, a request carrying both a session and a challenge cookie, a change landing between the two sign-in readings, a first reading that fails (refused).

`auth-manager-before-hook.ts`: holds. The readings sit after the lock gate, the reset subject is the one the non-spending resolver already computed, and the email door's lookup lowercases as the vendor's does; the phone door reuses `findPhoneSignInAccount`.

`auth-manager-after-hook.ts`: holds. Setting `returned` to the refusal before the settlement and throwing after it is consistent with `runAfterHooks`, which turns a thrown `APIError` into the response and keeps running the later hooks against a cleared `newSession`.

`invitation-mailbox-proof.ts`: holds; five lines, after the write and before `createSession`.

Tests: thirteen cases through the real routes plus one on the one-step door; each of the four claims has a case and a control, and the staging moves the clock past the first-credential window before any change.

S1 (should-fix) — `issuedBeforeChangeOf` answers "before" whenever the manager has no data engine. On an `AuthManager` built without `dataEngine` (the in-memory arm `createDatabaseConfig` warns about) every email-change link and every second-factor challenge is refused, for accounts that never changed a password. The same row is readable through `internalAdapter.findCredentialAccount`, the seam the two sign-in readings already use. Read the clock there, or name this arm in the changeset.

S2 (should-fix) — the sign-in cases pin status and code only, and allow a `set-auth-token` header on the refused answer (`if (raced.bearer) …`). The changeset says the door answers "what a wrong password answers". Pin that the refused answer carries no session token in its headers, or state that it may carry one for a session already ended.

S3 (should-fix) — "a check that cannot read its record refuses" is pinned for the clock as a unit only. No case drives a link, a challenge or a sign-in with an unreadable clock or a missing first reading, and none of the three ablation legs covers the `catch` in `issuedBeforeChangeOf` or the missing-reading arm of `refuseSignInAcrossCredentialChange`.

N1 (nit) — in `endEmailChangeTokenIssuedBeforeCredentialChange` the `import('jose')` shares a `try` with the decode, so a failed import leaves the request as it came, while the docblock says each check fails closed. `jose` is a declared dependency, so the arm is not expected to run.

N2 (nit) — `/two-factor/send-otp` is not among `TWO_FACTOR_VERIFY_PATHS`: a challenge opened before the change can still ask for a code there, though no verify door will take it.

N3 (nit) — the changeset describes the refused link as the one mailed "to the new address"; the code judges every token carrying `updateTo` (derived judgment 2).

No must-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/credential-change-ends-prior-access`
Reviewed-by: `isolated sub-agent of session_016WV4czt69hUUaG5XcgFNYL`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b5cbc6ad19fe850a64cb98c4bf553cbbb3d5a128`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/credential-change-ends-prior-access.md (declaration lines and the reworded claim), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-mailbox-proof.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/credential-change-ends-prior-access.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-one-step-acceptance-34257.test.ts + none in the diff beyond those; read, never reviewed: auth-manager-sign-in-lockout.ts, auth-manager-database-secret.ts, operator-password-reset.ts, platform-objects sys-account.object.ts, and better-auth 1.7.12 (db/internal-adapter, routes/sign-in, plugins/phone-number/routes) read from the published package source
Security-touching: yes

This record replaces the one on `4cb593b8cc0` (record 7024920025: PASS, S1 to S3, N1 to N3). It is a delta review of the three commits over that head (`04d44a601ea`, `b6285e3a27a`, `b5cbc6ad19f`: four files, the changeset, the rule module, the before-hook and the rule's test file), read on top of the whole-PR judgment already rendered. The whole-PR diff against merge base `eca20d22191` names the same eight files as before; the fix round added no file. Nothing was built, run or re-run. `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` is unchanged in the delta and stays the seat's at ACCEPT.

Gate verdicts on this head (check-run conclusions, read once): 41 `success`, 17 `skipped`, none `failure`. `Test Core`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` and one `Check Changeset` run conclude `success`. A second `Check Changeset` run was still `in_progress` when read (the PR body was edited after the push); the seat reads its conclusion before ACCEPT. Dev evidence on this head: plugin-auth 288/288 files, 6050 passed, 10 skipped; the rule's test file 17/17; dogfood battery exit 0, 482 files passed, 3 skipped, 4092 tests passed, no failures; five ablation legs, each red (unreadable-clock catch 2, missing first reading 1, phone first reading 2, clock and before-hook at their `4cb593b8cc0` versions 4, no session-cookie deletion 3).

### ① Derived judgments

The thirteen judgments of the prior record stand on this head. What the delta moves:

1. The clock's row. `readCredentialChangedAt` now reads `internalAdapter.findCredentialAccount(userId)`: the row with the user's id, provider `credential`, and `accountId` equal to the user's id. The prior head read the row by user and provider alone. Right, and tighter: this is the row the vendor itself checks a password against at both password doors (`routes/sign-in.mjs` filters on `accountId === user.id`; the phone door calls `findCredentialAccount`), and the row `updatePassword` writes. A credential row whose `accountId` is another value opens no password sign-in, so the clock no longer follows a row no door admits. Several rows on the exact triple are written together by `updatePassword`, so whichever one `findOne` answers carries the same stamp.
2. No data engine. The link and challenge checks no longer take the manager's engine. On a manager built without `dataEngine` they now judge by the same clock instead of refusing everything. Right; it removes a refusal the prior head gave to accounts that never changed a password.
3. The phone door's first reading is `ctx.context.adapter.findOne` on model `user`, field `phoneNumber`, an equality match on the body's number. Right: it is the vendor's own lookup at `/sign-in/phone-number`, statement for statement.
4. The changeset's first bullet now names both steps and both addresses of the email-change flow. Right: it matches the code, which judges every token carrying `updateTo`.
5. Public surface: `CredentialClockReader` is a new exported interface of a module nothing re-exports; `readCredentialChangedAt` changes its first parameter inside the package. No published export, schema key, request or response shape moves. Right.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and right: `@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, `fix(plugin-auth)!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in the changeset and still present on the PR body, the BREAKING paragraph, one ADR-0087 marker. The delta rewords one bullet and publishes nothing the level would follow.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Prior S1 to S3 and N1 to N3: answered in ④.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The clock is still one single-row read on equality predicates. It now returns the whole credential row where the prior head projected three fields; the reason is given in the docblock (the vendor's seam, so the clock needs no data engine), and the vendor reads the same row the same way on every password check. The phone reading is one single-row equality read. No in-app join, no id materialisation.
- Private residuals held by the security seat: R1, R2 — graded in the seat's private notes. Both are ruled and assigned to one follow-up change after this one lands; neither is graded must-fix for this PR.
- For the seat: the second `Check Changeset` run named above.

### ④ Design judgment

`credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts`: holds against the code it cites. `issuedBeforeChangeOf` refuses when the request carries no adapter with `findCredentialAccount`, and when the read throws. Read against `db/internal-adapter.mjs`, the reader is the three-predicate lookup the docblock names. Tried and not broken: a row on another `accountId` (answers "no row", and that row admits no sign-in), duplicate rows on the triple (one stamp), `Date` and string stamps (both pinned in the unit), a manager on the vendor's in-memory adapter (pinned through the routes).

`auth-manager-before-hook.ts`: holds. Both first readings go through the vendor's adapter; a lookup that throws is caught in `noteSignInCredential` and leaves no reading, which the second reading refuses. The now-unused import is removed.

`credential-change-ends-prior-access.test.ts`: 17 cases. The four added cases are driven through the real routes, and each carries a positive control.

Prior findings on this head:

- S1 — resolved. The clock and both first readings use the vendor's adapter; `the clock and the sign-in readings need no data engine` runs a manager with no `dataEngine` through a link that verifies, a link refused after a change, and both password doors.
- S2 — resolved. `handsOutSession` (a `set-auth-token` header, or a session cookie set to a value) is asserted `false` on the refused sign-in at both doors, beside `false` for a wrong password and `true` for the controls. The conditional assertion is gone.
- S3 — resolved. `a check that cannot read its record refuses`: a link, a challenge and a sign-in, each with the credential read failing, each compared with the never-issued, never-opened or wrong-password answer, each followed by its control. The ablation legs named above cover the `catch` and the missing-reading arm.
- N3 — done (derived judgment 4).
- N1 — kept as an accepted deviation; acceptable (`jose` is a declared dependency).
- N2 — kept as an accepted deviation; acceptable (the send door grants no access).

Fail-closed, path by path: no adapter, refuses; clock read throws, refuses; account lookup for a link throws, refuses; issue time missing, refuses once a change exists; challenge with no readable user, ended; first sign-in reading missing or unreadable, refused; second reading throws, refused. One arm answers the other way:

N4 (nit) — a credential row that is read but carries no parseable `updatedAt` answers "never changed" in `readCredentialChangedAt`, while the docblock says a record that cannot be read refuses. Present at both heads. `sys_account.updated_at` defaults to now and every password write stamps it, so a blank stamp means no write has happened; the wording, not the behaviour, is what is off.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
